## One decision, five unlocks. {#unlocks auto-animate="true"}

::: notes
"These aren't five features. They're five consequences of one decision."

1:40.

One note per click, each pinned to the part of the drawing it comes from.

1. Data vs. metadata: identity and history without moving a byte. Same values, same hash, on any machine.
2. Git + storage: review, concurrency and recovery we didn't have to invent. Pull before push; if something goes wrong it fails loudly, and repairs from git.
3. Reader vs. writer: you read with storage access alone. Every write is an attributed, reviewable commit.
4. Serverless, distributed: nothing to host. Point at the empty middle: there's no server between the two. Any laptop is a full client, and it fits inside the SCE you already run.
5. Open format: parquet and JSON, readable from any language. No lock-in, not even to datom.
:::
